meta.title: Tommaso Ferrario — Machine Learning Engineer
meta.description: Machine learning engineer at Intesa Sanpaolo, Milan. OCR and LLM pipelines in production, research in reinforcement learning and stochastic optimization.

hero.status: Trailhead · ML Engineer at Intesa Sanpaolo
hero.title: Hi, I'm Tommaso.
hero.lede: At Intesa Sanpaolo I build pipelines that read bank documents with OCR and LLMs. Before that I studied computer science at Milano-Bicocca, did research on reinforcement learning, and wrote my master's thesis on stochastic optimization at Stevens Institute of Technology in New Jersey.
ascent.title: The ascent so far · 2020 to present
routes.title: Routes completed
eorc.title: EORC Energy Optimization Platform
eorc.problem: Deciding how much energy capacity to build when future demand and supply are uncertain.
eorc.approach: The platform takes demand and supply scenarios and solves a multi-stage stochastic optimization problem to suggest capacity decisions. I designed the architecture and work on the optimization code, the backend and the frontend for exploring scenarios.
flood.title: FloodNet Image Segmentation
flood.problem: Find the flooded areas in drone images taken after Hurricane Harvey.
flood.approach: We trained U-Net, SegNet and DeepLab on the images and compared the results.
food.title: Fine-Grained Food Classification
food.problem: Recognize 251 kinds of food from photos, some of them low quality, with limited compute.
food.approach: A small pretrained CNN with only the last layer fine-tuned, and a KNN classifier on its features. Each image gets a quality check first, and degraded ones are restored with classical filters or a GAN.

travel.title: Travel Pals

tourist.title: Tourist Profiler
tourist.text: Reinforcement learning models that learn what a tourist likes and suggest places to visit. This became my AINA 2025 paper.
car.title: Self-Driving Car Simulation
car.text: A car in Unity that learns to drive with reinforcement learning, trained on tracks that get harder as it improves.
ants.title: Ant Interaction Networks
ants.text: Network analysis of which ants interact with which, to see how a colony organizes itself.
brain.title: Brain Tumor Detection from MRI
brain.text: Classifying MRI scans by whether they show a brain tumor.
tool.title: Mechanical Tool Classification
tool.text: We collected our own dataset of mechanical tool photos and built a pipeline to classify them, from preprocessing and segmentation to feature extraction.
camps.title: Base camps
intesa.title: Machine Learning Engineer
intesa.p1: I built and deployed an OCR + LLM pipeline that processes about 100,000 documents a month with 90% field-level accuracy, which cut down the time spent on manual review.
intesa.p2: I designed its architecture (Python, Kafka, PostgreSQL) and connected it to the bank’s existing systems. I also work with the business teams to turn their requirements into targets we can measure.
unimib.title: Research Fellow
unimib.org: Università degli Studi di Milano-Bicocca · Milan
unimib.p1: I built two reinforcement learning models, a hierarchical RL model and a Double DQN, that follow how a tourist’s interests change over time, and connected them to a recommendation engine. Python and Docker.
unimib.p2: The work became my first paper, published at AINA 2025 (Springer) with me as first author.
notes.title: Field notes
pub.title: Dynamic User Profiling for Personalized Tourism Recommendations Using Reinforcement Learning Models ↗
pub.authors: Ferrario, T., Fersini, E., Messina, E., Sormani, G.
pub.abstract: We propose two reinforcement learning models that update a user’s profile as their interests change, so the system can recommend better points of interest. One is a hierarchical RL model with matrix factorization, the other a Double Deep Q-Network. The hierarchical model works best for users with a long history, while the DDQN does better with new or less active users.
